title: Ops + Sales: Speedrun Battlebrief (WIP)
audience: Sales engineers, field sellers, ops on-call
objective: Give an ultra-compact, ops-aware battlebrief for first 10 minutes with a prospect: qualify fast, handle 3 top technical objections, and prepare a pilot rescue plan if things go sideways.
abstract: Working draft. This one-pager + speaker notes is aimed at enabling quick reaction in discovery and pilot kickoff. Focus: shorten negotiation friction by surfacing operational guarantees, fallback modes, and a compact demo script that showcases latency/cost controls and deterministic rollback options.
core_messages: Redwood is built for predictable inference: measurable latency SLOs + cost levers that teams actually use.
We provide staged deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private) with the same API and rollout primitives so customers can migrate without rewriting top-level orchestration.
Fallback-first design: automatic model variant fallback + region failover to keep apps live under load/constraints.
Pilot safety: pilot contracts + escape hatches (rate limits, model pins, graceful degrade) reduce procurement anxiety and accelerate buy-in.
three_minute_pitch: Problem: LLM features promise value but are fragile in production — latency spikes, cost overruns, and unpredictable fallbacks cause product teams to stall.
What we do: Redwood gives engineers a single API to serve models with predictable latency, transparent cost breakdowns, and operational controls to mitigate risk.
Why it matters to them: Faster time-to-value for pilots, predictable billing for budgeting, and clear escape hatches for compliance and reliability.
demo_script_bullets: 0:00–0:30 — One-line customer pain acknowledgement + 30s Redwood value prop (latency, cost, reliability).
0:30–1:30 — Live call: generate a short customer-facing reply (use model X-small) showing sub-200ms tail on our hosted region — highlight token/time counters in Console.
1:30–2:30 — Show Console: per-route latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens, prefix cache hit rate. Point to 'Optimize' suggestions for batch/quantization.
2:30–4:00 — Failure scenario demo: simulate overloaded capacity -> automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant, show preserved 95th latency SLO with reduced quality (annotate fallback reason).
4:00–5:00 — Pilot ask: 2-week trial, sample dataset, simple success metrics (median latency <200ms, cost < $X per 1k tokens, accuracy threshold Y).
top_technical_objections_and_responses: Objection: "The model output quality drops when you quantize or fallback." — Response: "We provide comparative evals on your prompt set and a canary that measures regression signals; rollbacks are single-click and pinned to the previous model variant."

Objection: "We can’t expose data to hosted APIs." — Response: "Private deployment options with customer-controlled VPC and KMS/HSM integrations; same API and telemetry but data never leaves your network."
Objection: "Latency spikes under bursty traffic." — Response: "Dedicated pools + autoscaling policies and burst capacity; smart routing will route by latency SLO and region to maintain tail bounds."
pilot_rescue_playbook: Prep: create a pilot runbook pre-approved with customer including success metrics and SLA budget
Tiered controls: pre-provision reserved capacity, establish model pins and an agreed fallback model list
Monitoring: enable 1-min resolution tracing for first 72 hours and set regression alerts on eval prompt sets
Escalation: on >2x tail latency, enable immediate route to fallback variant and notify SE + platform-on-call via Slack incident channel
Postmortem: capture token-level cost delta, error traces, and prompt examples that triggered fallback for a follow-up tuning session
pricing_anchors_and_negotiation_cues: Anchor: typical pilot footprint — 20k tokens/day -> suggest hosted with reserved burst credit for first 30 days to limit unpredictable billing.
Discount cue: for committed dedicated capacity we can offer a 10–20% unit discount and predictable SLA-based credits.
Operational credit: include 5 hours of SE onboarding + one smoke-test canary in the pilot to lower friction.
one_page_fallback_matrix: Normal: hosted model A -> Latency SLO met -> continue
High latency: route to regional replica or model B (smaller), enable cache-only responses for repeat prefixes
Capacity shortfall: degrade to non-streaming batching with prefetch, show user partial replies and estimated ETA
Security requirement: route to private deployment or private-only model variants
speaker_notes_quick_tips: Callouts: always surface the customer's main constraint first (latency vs cost vs compliance). Tailor the demo to their constraint.
Use numbers: share 95th percentile latency and per-1k-token cost numbers from Console — customers respond to concrete tradeoffs.
Probe: ask if they have a strict SLA or internal cost cap. That determines hosted vs dedicated path immediately.
Fail-safe language: 'We can pin model X at time t and automatically roll back if quality drops' is reassuring — practice the rollback CLI flow once before demos.
